title: Split+
tagline: Split parts, surfaces, curves or faces with several tools. Optionally supply reference geometry from which we can establish a more stable definition of which side of the geometry to split we intend to keep or remove

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: The built-in Split keeps "front" or "back" of one tool. That choice is tied to the tool's normal, which flips whenever an upstream loft, offset, mirror or sketch changes. Split+ splits by many tools at once and names the side to keep with geometry: a reference that lies on that side.
useWhen: A body must be cut by several planes or surfaces in one step
You keep one side, and the tools' normals may change upstream
Later features need the pieces by position: start, middle, end
slides.caption: Split+ open on a ski topsheet: the target and the two tools (Station A and B) highlight.

slides.title: Why a reference instead of a flip

points.head: A flip is about a normal
points.body: 'Keep front' means the side the tool's normal points to -- and normals change freely upstream.

points.head: A reference is about the model
points.body: Pick geometry on the side you mean. The choice survives any change of orientation.

points.head: Drop-in
points.body: With no reference, Split+ behaves exactly like the built-in Split.

points.head: Signed distance
points.body: For each tool: s = (P - C) . n at the closest point. s > 0: the reference is in front of the tool.

points.head: Per tool
points.body: Each tool keeps the reference's side (box on) or the other side (box off). What survives is on the reference's side of every tool.

points.head: No reference
points.body: Behaves like the built-in: on = each tool's front, off = its back.

points.head: Pick tools in order
points.body: 1 tool: near / far (or front / back). 2 tools: start, middle, end. 3+: start, middle1..N-1, end.

points.head: Orientation never matters
points.body: 'Forward' for each tool is the side the next tool is on.

points.head: Crossing tools
points.body: The split is made as asked; region keys are published empty, with an info notice.

slides.title: The dialog: split, keep both sides
params: Split type
PART: split whole bodies. FACE: split only the picked faces; nothing is removed.
Parts, surfaces, or curves to split
The targets. Every target is split by every tool.
Entities to split with
Surfaces, faces, planes or mate connectors, in pick order. Pick them in order along the part: region names follow it.
Keep tools
Keep sheet-body tools after the split.
Trim to face boundaries
A single-face tool cuts only within its own boundary, as the built-in.
Keep both sides
On (default): every piece is kept and sorted into regions. Off: keep one side per tool (next slide).
Debug
Print sides: which side of each tool the reference is on, and what was kept.

slides.title: The dialog: keep one side
params: Keep both sides
Off: each tool keeps one side.
Side reference
Geometry on the side to keep -- best a mate connector or vertex inside the region you want. Here: Mid (x 900).
Keep side nearest reference
The arrow. On: keep the side of each tool the reference is on. Off: keep the other side. Without a reference: each tool's front / back.
slides.note: Result: only the region between Station A and B survives, whatever way the two planes face (example 2).

slides.title: The dialog: face split
params: Split type
FACE: split only the picked faces. Nothing is removed; the pieces stay part of their body.
Faces to split
The faces to split. Planes and mate connectors cut them infinitely; surfaces cut as they are.
Side reference
Optional. With one tool it names the two regions near / far; it never removes anything here.
slides.note: Regions are published as faces: pick 'middle' in Extract variables to fillet or offset only those faces.

slides.title: Example 1: three regions
slides.head: Topsheet split at Station A (x 300) and B (x 1500), Keep both sides on
slides.body: Nothing is removed. The three pieces are published as start (x -19..300), middle (300..1500) and end (1500..1799), and the cut edges as splitEdges -- one edge per cut: 9 edges, 5 at A and 4 at B.

slides.title: Example 2: keep only the middle
slides.head: VOLUME_STD split at Station A and B, Keep both sides off, Side reference = Mid (x 900)
slides.body: Each station plane keeps the side Mid is on, so only the part between A and B survives (green); the tip and tail pieces (grey) are removed. Flipping either plane's normal changes nothing -- which the built-in 'keep front / back' cannot promise.

slides.title: Example 3: split faces, not bodies
slides.head: Face split: the SW_SHELF faces (the shelf along the sidewall) cut at Station A and B
slides.body: Nothing is removed and no new body is made: the shelf faces are divided at A and B and published as regions -- start 4 faces, middle 9, end 4. A later feature (a fillet, an offset, a Thicken+) can then work on 'middle' alone, and keeps working when the stations move.

slides.title: Outputs: what Extract variables can publish
keys: The pieces in each region: bodies (solids, surfaces or curves) in a Part split, faces in a Face split.
A region's edges except the cuts (for a surface: its open boundary).
start + end together / every middle region together.

The NEW edges along each cut line -- where a tool crosses a target. Keeping both sides leaves two coincident copies of every cut edge; only one is published. Input edges that were merely cut in two are not included.
splitEdges sorted by the tool that made them (each edge goes to its nearest tool): 1 tool: cut; 2 tools: startCut, endCut; 3+: cut1..cutN. Topsheet example: startCut = the 5 edges at x 300.
The cap faces the split created on solids (empty for surfaces and in a Face split).
Numbers: pieces left; regions the tools define (N + 1 for N tools).

slides.title: Messages
messages: A tool is also a target
The keep side reference lies on tool k
Move the reference clearly to one side of that tool.
No part of the targets is on the kept side of every tool.
Tools cross, or were picked out of order. The split itself is fine.

items.head: Use a local reference
items.body: A mate connector or vertex inside the region to keep. A far plane can read the wrong side where the part curves.

items.head: Reference regions, not indices
items.body: Extract variables can publish 'middle' or 'startCut'; those names survive changes upstream.

items.head: Edge tools are not offered
items.body: The side rule needs a surface. Use the built-in Split for projected edges.

items.head: How pieces are sorted into regions
items.body: Split+ checks which side of each tool ONE point of each piece lies on (its centre; for a face, the nearest point on the face). A piece that curls back across a tool's extended plane could land in the wrong region -- check regions with Show in Extract variables.
